body:
Updated to c74d888d (still a draft):

- **#1615's review fix merged in** (4f05e9c0 at 3b532fac). Conflicts in both `run_job` mark-law call sites: the mark law still picks its mesh (the source part, or on a stock source the setup's parts) and hands it to the one `mark_into`, now returning `Marked`, with `mark_law::notes` in both frame arms - so #1615's `MARK_FLOOR` / `seat_skin` floor and the unlowered shank/holder stack check apply to a stock-source Engrave / Trace too. Pinned by `mark_floor.rs::a_stock_source_cut_through_the_plate_meets_the_same_floor` (red with the skin emptied). The stack line now reads "review only the commits after 4f05e9c0".
- **#1621 (P1) fixed on this branch:** a part-source op that carries a part law is also judged against the setup's other parts (`keep_law::neighbour_parts`) with the plain solid law (no mark budget), in both frame arms; its own source keeps its own law. Before: a 0.3 mm mark on B whose flank took 2.3 mm off A posted on BOTH stocks (the sim credits A the budget too - #1627); a Contour into A posted on a turned stock. Pins in `neighbour_law.rs` (5) plus the 3+2 arm in `area_controls.rs`; mutation table in the body.
- Two existing tests changed for #1621 (reasons in the body and the decision file): `area_controls` tilted-pocket comparison runs without the tower the tilted offset really enters; `stock_source_verdict` regenerates after marking the casting raw stock only.
- **Filed:** #1627 (P7, sim mark credit on a neighbour) and #1628 (P1, the op's stamp does not follow the parts beside its source: a part moved into the cut after generation posts on a turned stock). A stamp term was built and pinned here, then taken back out because it re-states established stamp contracts; #1628 has the options.
- Gate: quick green on c74d888d; clippy clean.

Quick pass @ c74d888d (stacked on #1615 - review only the commits after 4f05e9c0; merge #1615 first): quick gate green, `clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings` clean; body complete (both jobs, pins + mutation table, changed tests named, Changelog, Fixes #1607 and #1621). Follow-ups #1628 (P1, needs a maintainer decision on stamp rules) and #1627 (P7). Flagged ready for review (safety tier: P1).

Note from SKULL's #1628 worker (PR #1643, stacked on this one), not verified here: a tap's generation-time core acquittal looks like it also drops gouges against neighbour parts, not only against its own source. If that's right, a tapped hole that enters a neighbouring part reads clean at generation. #1643's live re-judge at post is stricter for taps, but only on a turned stock. Worth a look in this PR's review.
